companyRankingLists.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
companyRankingLists.itemDescription:
Progressive’s Inclusion Quarterly initiative features speakers and discussion groups, and encourages storytelling and sharing. A weeklong inclusion program in 2022 attracted 32,269 employees, who attended programming on topics such as thriving in a digital workplace and using emotional intelligence to nurture relationships and trust.
 

Since its workplace shifted to 90% remote and hybrid over the pandemic, the insurer’s staff have increasingly relied on its intracompany social media platform to connect and share stories; 4,500 employees joined the platform in 2022.
 

Every Progressive worker is eligible to recommend that any charity receive a $100 donation from the Progressive Insurance Foundation. In 2023 the company expanded its donation program to include national nonprofit Family Promise, which, alongside Progressive’s ongoing collaboration with the Cleveland operations of Humble Design, represents the company’s particular commitment to ending homelessness in the U.S.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription:
A leading provider of auto, vehicle, and homeowner insurance in the U.S., Progressive says that 96% of its employees agree with the following statement: “When you join the company, you are made to feel welcome.”

  • Within the past two years, Progressive says, it has increased the representation of people of color among senior leadership from 13% to 17%. And at the end of 2022, it says, 45% of those in leadership positions were women and 25% were people of color.

  • The Multicultural Leadership Development Program is a 12-to-18-month training to help higher-performing employees prepare for managerial positions.

  • All employees have access to PrudentRx, which lets members avoid out-of-pocket expenses for all approved specialty medications in Progressive’s health plan.

  • “They are transparent and seek to create a work environment where people of all backgrounds can collaborate and work together. I truly feel valued and appreciated,” said one employee.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription:
The fifth largest property and casualty insurer in the Fortune 500, Progressive’s performance in 2022 was mixed, with a 4% increase in revenue but a 79% decrease in profit compared to the prior year, and it dropped nine places on the Fortune 500.

  • Auto claims stabilized in 2022 after first dropping in 2020 because of stay-at-home initiatives and then jumping up in 2021 as drivers returned to the road.

  • Hurricane Ian, which struck Florida and South Carolina in September 2022, ate into Progressive’s bottom line. For all insurers, the massive storm caused the second-largest insured loss on record after Hurricane Katrina in 2005.

  • Progressive is one of the 52 Fortune 500 companies that have women leaders, with Tricia Griffith as president and CEO. Progressive is one of the few companies with a female board chair: Lawton W. Fitt, a retired Goldman Sachs partner.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: Progressive is the third-largest auto insurance carrier in the U.S. by market share, and the largest insurer of commercial vehicles. As more cars got back on the road in 2021, the economy’s rebound from the pandemic was a mixed blessing for Progressive. The company recorded an 11% year-over-year revenue increase, but a 41% year-over-year decrease in profits—since more driving meant more accidents and more insurance claims.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: Though drivers were stuck at home for much of the year, Progressive’s business remained in high gear. The company did not lay off or furlough workers, and even offered personal auto customers 20% rebates in May and June of 2020. One employee appreciated that Progressive modified its bonus schedule to pay out quarterly rather than at year-end, a move that helped families who might have experienced a job loss. Says one veteran of the Fortune 500 company, led by Tricia Griffith, who was Fortune’s 2018 Businessperson of the Year: “Progressive is by far the best place I’ve ever worked.”

companyRankingLists.title: Fortune Global 500
companyRankingLists.itemDescription: Car travel may have all but stalled for much of 2020, but Progressive nonetheless gained a windfall of business—with policies increasing by 2.4 million and an additional $3 billion in net premiums written over the prior year. The company’s agency auto business and Uber and Lyft premiums decreased because of shelter-in-place restrictions and decreased circulation. Yet the insurer’s commercial lines business saw significant growth in the for-hire transportation business, spurred on by increased demand for shipping services.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: Progressive had a big year: With revenues climbing 22% year-over-year, profits jumping 52%, and more than 4,000 new employees hired, the insurer catapulted up 68 spots on the Global 500. Progressive’s growth was aided by its commercial lines segment, which grew 20% year-over-year. The House that Flo Built also expanded its auto coverage with ridesharing titans Uber and Lyft. In early 2020, stay-at-home orders dramatically lowered domestic traffic, and thus auto insurance claims. As a result, CEO Tricia Griffith—who, in 2018, was the first woman to be named Fortune’s Businessperson of the Year—announced that the company would refund its insured drivers 20% of their April and May premiums.
